summary: The retained test's writer thread drove BEGIN IMMEDIATE/COMMIT/ROLLBACK by hand via sqlite3_exec in a busy-retry loop with SQL built via string concatenation -- the exact pattern this same branch's own governance ledger (3210-mgmt-group-backfill-torn-read.lAnfBW.jsonl, finding MG-3) already graded BLOCKING when found in the OTHER (removed, unauthorized) test. MG-3 was dispositioned fixed by deleting that test, which removed one instance of the pattern and left its twin in the retained test unchecked.
trigger: a std::bad_alloc during per-iteration SQL string concatenation inside the writer thread's retry loop, or any early exit leaving the manual transaction unclosed
policy_floor: manual resource cleanup in new C++ not RAII-wrapped, applied here for consistency with MG-3's own disposition on the identical pattern in the same PR
classification_rationale: a code defect in test infrastructure, not a doc/comment contradiction
provenance: introduced (missed during MG-3's own remediation -- only the OTHER test was checked for this pattern)

summary: The test never asserted the writer's swap actually landed -- migrate_done was the only cross-thread signal, so a run where migrate_from_sqlite finished before the writer ever committed passed every assertion without exercising the race at all. (I6: coverage/reachability gap, matching the same shape as sibling findings MG-11/DG-3/G8-6 in this PR's earlier round -- not I3, since the fix itself was never wrong, only the test's ability to detect a regression was intermittently absent.) Independently corroborated by a static finding from a second reviewer (Codex) and by the ledger's own MG-4 finding (retained test's catch rate ~12%, weaker than the removed test's). Fixed via a writer_swap_done atomic, set only in the transaction's own success path, required after join(). Empirically re-measured (not assumed): the fix also raised the catch rate from 3/25 to 8/25 on a fresh negative control -- a genuine improvement, not merely defensive insurance.
trigger: the writer thread never landing a commit before migrate_done is observed (empirically rare in practice -- 0/20 measured after the fix -- but structurally possible and previously unguarded)
classification_rationale: a test-quality defect (vacuous-pass risk), not a doc/comment contradiction

summary: The comment (already corrected once this round for overclaiming, per MG-16) now undersold the fix in the opposite direction: it described the defect as solely a nondeterministic FK-triggered refusal. A member moved between two groups that BOTH continue to exist tears across tables without tripping any FK (both group_ids stay valid references) -- a genuinely silent, FK-invisible inconsistency the transaction also closes, not just the FK-visible refusal case the comment named.
trigger: a reader relying on the comment's claim that a torn read here always either succeeds cleanly or fails closed via the FK
classification_rationale: the fix's own correctness and BLOCKING status are unaffected -- the transaction closes both failure classes regardless of which one the comment named; only the comment's completeness was at issue
provenance: introduced (a second miscalibration of the same comment within this PR, opposite direction from MG-16's overclaim)

summary: PASS items independently re-verified by the reviewer and not disputed: the production transaction-wrap itself (BEGIN/SqliteTxn placement, checked commit, rollback-on-early-return, correct declaration order); the deferred-vs-BEGIN-IMMEDIATE choice (reviewer verified the snapshot pins at the corruption probe, the first real read, not merely 'read-only connection' as the comment implies); the pure-addition diff shape; the sibling-store verdicts (management_group_store 3-table, others 1-table); the provenance disclosure's accuracy; CI green including an independent 25x race-test run against live Postgres (25/25, matching the PR's own 0/25 claim).
